text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Moslem-Croat Federation remains open to all options to resolve Bosnia's debt payment default to the World Bank, the co-chairman of the Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, says. The necessary funds might be lent to Bosnia's Serb entity.
- Investigators have exhumated 71 bodies so far from a mass grave site in a Sarajevo cemetery in the village of Vlakovo, which was transferred to federation control last year.
- Mirza Hajric, aide to presidency chairman Alija Izetbegovic, declines to confirm Croatian and Bosnian presidents are due to meet this month in Croatia as reported recently by Croatian media.
- The federation parliament's House of People is due to discuss on Tuesday laws on the budget, forming new municipalities and sale of apartments with tenancy rights.

- Three attorneys from Tuzla, with assistance from the International Human Rights Law Group, filed an appeal with a Bosnian Serb court in Zvornik for the retrial of Moslem defendants known as the "Zvornik seven". The men say they are innocent and that Serb authorities denied them a fair trial. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
